title: Can't remap CTRL (Left) + Shift (Right) to Disabled

status.label: Confirm modifier-only shortcut disabling on current release
status.detail: The report says Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right) cannot be mapped to Disabled while ordinary shortcuts work; related issue 31094 tracks a broader modifier-only remapping request.

judgment.rationale: The reporter lists PowerToys 0.80.1 on Windows 11 and gives a specific modifier-only combination, Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right), that fails when mapped to Disabled while combinations containing ordinary keys can be remapped. A commenter says it appears to be the same issue as #31094, which tracks inability to remap modifier-only shortcuts, but current behavior and whether the two different-side modifiers are the same limitation are unconfirmed.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.80.1 and Windows 11 with Spanish and English configurations.
The attempted action is Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right) to Disabled; combinations such as Ctrl+J and Ctrl+Alt+comma reportedly work.
A commenter identifies #31094 as a likely same issue; #31094 remains open and covers modifier-only shortcut remapping generally.
The issue is open and unassigned; no linked fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the exact modifier-only action is still rejected on current stable and whether #31094's general modifier-only scenario covers it; avoid treating it as fixed by an unrelated similar issue.

fix_assessment.rationale: If current builds still reject the mapping, Keyboard Manager may prohibit modifier-only triggers for Disable actions or reject the combination because it overlaps an OS/input-language shortcut. Current rules and behavior need confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Allow supported modifier-only shortcuts to be disabled
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Disable action may reject modifier-only triggers even when the user intends to suppress a specific Ctrl/Shift combination. Alternatively, Windows may reserve the combination for input-language switching; the report does not establish which rule blocks it.
plan: Confirm the exact combination and rejection on current stable, including whether the target app changes the result.
Compare with the broader modifier-only case tracked by #31094 and check whether the action is OS-reserved.
If the combination is not reserved and is a supported trigger, update Disable-action validation to accept it.
Add regression tests for left/right-specific modifier-only triggers and rejected reserved combinations.
verification: Verify Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right) can be disabled when the target combination is supported.
Verify the mapping does not suppress unrelated Ctrl/Shift combinations.
Verify genuinely reserved system shortcuts remain rejected with a clear explanation.

confidence.rationale: The exact rejected mapping and successful ordinary-key comparisons are useful, but current validation behavior and OS reservation are unknown.

issue_context.summary: The Disable action reportedly rejects Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right), while shortcuts containing ordinary keys are accepted.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.80.1 on Windows 11 with Spanish and English configurations.
Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right) to Disabled is rejected; Ctrl+J and Ctrl+Alt+comma can be remapped.
A commenter says the report may be the same as #31094, an open issue about modifier-only shortcut remapping.
inferences: The combination may be blocked by modifier-only validation or by an OS-reserved input-language shortcut; the report does not distinguish them.
issue_context.analysis: The current validation rules need confirmation before classifying this as a bug or an intentional limitation. #31094 is relevant tracking context but is not a linked fix.
initial_investigation: Read the report and both comments, including the exact mapping and comparison shortcuts.
Reviewed #31094, which remains open and describes modifier-only shortcut remapping generally; no covering fix is linked.

information_gaps.information: Whether the exact Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right) to Disabled mapping is still rejected on current stable, and whether it is an OS-reserved shortcut
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the failure is current and whether the mapping should be accepted or clearly rejected as reserved.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On current stable, recreate the exact mapping and report the PowerToys version, whether the same behavior occurs in a target app, and whether Windows uses the combination for input-language switching.

comment.body: Thanks for specifying Ctrl (Left)+Shift (Right) to Disabled and the ordinary-key combinations that do work. Could you confirm whether the exact modifier-only mapping is still rejected on current stable PowerToys, include the version, and say whether Windows uses that combination for input-language switching? This will help distinguish validation limits from an OS-reserved shortcut.
